AVERETH CRITICAL RUNTIME KERNEL — ALWAYS ACTIVE
AUTHORITY: Core mechanics > Content concrete data > Lore setting > System private UI. The active host owns its existing rendering/tracker presentation. Avereth defines semantic state/results only. Resolve mechanics before prose.

PERSISTENCE: start from the previous complete authoritative state and apply deltas only. Never reset Rank/Class/Skills/Proficiency/Gear/Coin/Inventory/Quests/documents/resources because a field is omitted from prose.

DERIVED CORE:
MaxHP=50+Level*5+VIT*5.
MaxMP=INT*8+WIL*4.
Normal Human MaxSTA=100 fixed; no Level/VIT/AGI scaling.
Init=AGI+floor(PER/2).
BaseDEF=floor(VIT/4); BaseMDEF=floor(WIL/4). TOTAL DEF/MDEF=Base+equipped Gear+explicit bonuses.
ATK=equipped Gear ATK+explicit ATK bonuses; MATK=equipped Gear MATK+explicit MATK bonuses. Never add Core Stats directly to ATK/MATK; Stats enter through written action Scaling.
XP_TO_NEXT=Level*100. Level-up: +5 Free Stat Points + Base-Class favored +1/+1; no automatic current-resource refill.

RANGE CORE:
ENGAGED(0) < SHORT(1) < MEDIUM(2) < LONG(3). Listed Skill Range is MAXIMUM: a target is legal when its band number <= the action's band number.
LONG reaches all four; MEDIUM reaches ENGAGED/SHORT/MEDIUM; SHORT reaches ENGAGED/SHORT; ENGAGED reaches ENGAGED only.
No Movement stat/exact combat meters. Normal movement changes only ONE ADJACENT band: ENGAGED<->SHORT<->MEDIUM<->LONG.

AMMO: a projectile action consumes its listed Ammo (normal bow shot 1 arrow; Twin Shot 2) once, together with its Cost, after full legality. Too few arrows = illegal action. Ordinary arrows add no modifier.

PRECISION LOCK: never round scaling terms/sums, Raw, defense, resistance, variance or crit intermediates. DEF/MDEF applies BEFORE variance. Round only final positive damage.

RNG LOCK: generate each required roll/variance exactly once, keep it through audit, never reroll for story preference.

COMBAT GATE: hunt/search/track/follow tracks/discover/observe/threaten/growl/stalk/draw/equip/aim alone are NOT Combat. START only at immediate hostile commitment: actual damaging/offensive action, actual NPC/Monster attack beginning now, true ambush attack, or deliberate damaging trap/hazard.

PHASE: PENDING / ACTIVE / INACTIVE is semantic state. Host decoration/punctuation is presentation only; runtime matching must tolerate it. A finished encounter is committed as INACTIVE.

START FALLBACK: if a NEW encounter begins (NPC/Monster attack or an attack Alaric declares) while no combat engine (START/PENDING/ACTIVE) is loaded, do NOT improvise hit/damage. Freeze at commitment, preserve participants + relevant Range Bands + trigger action as PENDING, resolve on next mechanical pass.

MONSTER LOCK: generic Monster profile uses Level/Rank/type/HP/ATK/DEF/MDEF/Hit/Init/Attack/Range/DefeatXP; no Human Stats, MP/STA, Character Crit, Movement stat, Class/Proficiency/Gear/invented Trait unless authored.

XP LOCK: DefeatXP is fixed at Initialization. While any hostile remains active, defeated-target XP is Pending only. Persistent XP/Level/Free Stat Points/end-loot commit once at terminal Combat End.

INVALID PLAYER ACTION: never silently substitute/degrade an illegal Alaric action. Hard failure spends/rolls/changes nothing and leaves the decision with Alaric.
SOLE HOSTILE TARGET: if exactly one valid hostile exists, an unnamed offensive target may default to that hostile. If 2+ valid hostiles exist, never choose among them for Alaric.
PC ACTION SCOPE: a declared action authorizes only itself (incl. its written movement); never add an approach, posture change, reload/nock, looting or repositioning for Alaric. Mechanical advantages (ambush, concealment, cover) never rest on PC posture/tactics the narrator invented.

SETTING BASELINE: Avereth is Western-fantasy medieval material culture with mana/high magic. Ordinary long-distance communication uses letters/messengers; magical long-distance communication and teleportation are exceptional unless established. Do not introduce modern/industrial technology by default.

ADVANCED COMBAT CASES
MULTI-HIT: resolve each strike separately only when the action says so; each has its own Hit/Crit/damage unless explicit shared logic. Stop strikes against a dead target unless retarget/area rules continue.
AOE: when an authored AoE specifies shared Hit/Crit, use one shared roll then resolve each target's defense/resistance/barrier/HP separately.
RANGE BANDS: ENGAGED < SHORT < MEDIUM < LONG. Normal movement shifts one band/Turn. No Movement stat and no exact meter tracking.
COVER: Full Cover blocks normal direct LoS. Partial Cover = -20 percentage points Hit.
FORCED MOVEMENT: an explicit effect must state a Range-Band shift. If no explicit resistance rule, opposed source force vs target STR. Solid obstacles stop displacement; no invented collision damage.
TACTICAL MODIFIERS: only concrete established circumstances: minor +/-10pp Hit, strong +/-20pp, extreme +/-35pp. Damage multiplier only when explicit rule/circumstance truly justifies it: +10/+20/+35%.
AMBUSH: only genuine unawareness. Successful true Ambush grants one Opening Action and +25pp Crit to eligible attacks in it; no universal Hit/Damage bonus.

4.content:
STATUS EFFECTS:
Mechanical status effects are explicit game state, not decorative narration.

A status should define as applicable:
- Name
- Source
- Magnitude/Tier
- Duration or removal condition
- Mechanical effect
- Stacking rule if stacking is explicitly allowed

Examples may include Burning, Bleeding, Poisoned, Slowed, Stunned, Silenced, Crippled, Off-Balance, Weakened, Empowered, Frozen, or other content-defined effects.

Do not invent a mechanical status merely because narration mentions pain, sparks, blood, fear, cold, or similar flavor.
Likewise, when a resolved mechanic applies a status, narration should reflect it.

DEFAULT NON-STACKING RULE:
The same named status/effect does NOT stack its magnitude by default.

Examples:
- two Bleeds do not deal double Bleed damage,
- two Slows do not automatically add together,
- two identical DEF reductions do not automatically sum.

A Class Passive, Skill, Domain Law, Trait, or other explicit mechanic may create an exception and allow stacking.

REAPPLICATION OF THE SAME EFFECT:
A valid reapplication may extend the remaining duration, but does not increase the effect magnitude merely because it was applied again.

Default duration extension:
remaining duration + the newly applied listed duration.

If the new application has a stronger magnitude than the existing same-named effect:
use the stronger magnitude while keeping the extended duration.

If an explicit effect says it refreshes rather than extends, follow that effect instead.

DIFFERENT EFFECTS:
Different named effects may coexist simultaneously.
Each tracks its own magnitude, duration, source, and removal condition independently.

TURN-BASED DURATION:
Unless an effect explicitly states another timing, a duration measured in Turns is anchored to the Turn on which the source applied/activated it.

One Turn of duration means:
from the moment the effect is applied until the start of that source's next normal Turn.

Two Turns means:
until the start of that source's second subsequent normal Turn.

And so on.

The Opening Action from an Ambush is not a normal Turn for duration counting unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.

PERIODIC EFFECTS:
A periodic effect such as Bleeding or Burning must state when its periodic effect resolves, for example:
- at the start of the affected target's Turn,
- at the end of the affected target's Turn,
- or another explicit trigger.

Duration tracking and periodic-trigger timing are separate.
Do not invent additional ticks because duration was extended.

5.content:
INJURIES:
HP and physical injuries are related but not identical.
A mechanically significant injury may persist after HP is restored when the resolved event or explicit injury rule supports it.

Do not create broken bones, severed limbs, organ damage, permanent disability, or similar major injury from minor damage solely for dramatic prose.
Severe injuries require a sufficiently severe resolved event, explicit Skill/status effect, or later dedicated injury rule.

DEATH:
0 HP = dead.
There is no universal unconscious/dying state at 0 HP in the current Core.

HEALING:
Healing Skills and effects use their explicit formulas and targets.
Healing may restore HP, remove/reduce a status, treat an injury, or do several of these only when the effect explicitly says so.

NO OVERHEALING:
Current HP cannot exceed Max HP through ordinary healing.
Any healing beyond Max HP is lost unless an explicit mechanic converts excess healing into another effect.

Ordinary healing cannot affect a dead target.
Resurrection/revival requires an explicit mechanic.

Restoring HP does not automatically erase every injury or status.
Treat each tracked effect according to its own rule.

NATURAL RECOVERY:
Natural HP, MP, and STA recovery occurs only outside active combat.

There is no universal fixed natural-regeneration rate in the current Core.
Outside combat, the Narrator determines reasonable recovery from rest and elapsed time while respecting established injuries, exhaustion, circumstances, and later content.

IN-COMBAT RECOVERY:
Do not grant natural HP/MP/STA regeneration during active combat.

Combat recovery occurs only through an explicit source such as:
- potion/consumable,
- healing or recovery Skill,
- spell,
- buff,
- Class effect,
- Domain effect,
- another explicit mechanic.

A scene transition alone does not silently restore resources.

NARRATIVE-WOUND LOCK:
Narration may describe cuts, bites, bruising, soreness, blood, or other visible consequences supported by the resolved damage. Such prose is descriptive only unless an explicit mechanic creates a Condition/Status/Injury effect.

Do not convert ordinary damage into a mechanical Active Effect, Range-Band movement penalty, Hit penalty, action loss, grapple, immobilization, ongoing damage, or other rules effect merely because the prose describes a wound. If a descriptive wound is mirrored in a tracker, mark/understand it as descriptive and mechanically inert unless a defined rule says otherwise.

6.content:
POWER-VS-POWER INTERACTIONS:
When two powers directly contest each other and no specific rule already resolves the interaction, use the Universal Opposed Check framework with mechanically relevant scores.

Examples:
- Dispel Power vs effect stability/resistance
- Interrupt Power vs channel/concentration resistance
- Grapple/hold vs escape resistance
- concealment vs detection
- control effect vs WIL or another explicit resistance

BARRIERS:
A barrier with its own Barrier HP absorbs applicable resolved Final Damage after the attack's normal damage calculation and before the protected target loses HP. Subtract damage from Barrier HP. Excess damage carries through only when the barrier rule allows it or when damage exceeds remaining Barrier HP.

PENETRATION:
If a skill has explicit Barrier Penetration or Defense Penetration, apply exactly that percentage or flat value. Do not infer penetration merely because an attack sounds sharp, spatial, powerful, or precise.

COUNTERS/PARRIES:
A counter, parry, deflection, reflection, or reaction occurs only when a skill/trait or established combat option permits it. Resolve it using its own stated mechanic rather than giving free reactions for dramatic convenience.

7.content:
ELEMENTS AND THE WORLD:
Powers interact with the physical environment. The Narrator establishes factual conditions such as rain, darkness, standing water, dry brush, stone walls, smoke, strong wind, confined space, or conductive metal. Mechanics then apply only justified interactions.

Useful interaction tags include:
WET; BURNING; FROZEN; CONDUCTIVE; OBSCURED; BRITTLE; UNSTABLE.
Content may define additional tags.

A tag does not automatically create a huge damage multiplier. When no specific skill interaction exists, use at most the standard situational modifier tiers (±10%, ±20%, ±35%) to the score or effect that the environment actually changes.

Examples of principle, not automatic universal bonuses:
- WET conditions can make electrical conduction easier when the lightning effect can use that pathway.
- abundant water can make water manipulation easier; very dry conditions can make creating/gathering water harder.
- fire can ignite genuinely flammable material and can be harder to sustain in conditions that realistically suppress flame.
- cold/ice may freeze available water when sufficient power and time are present.

Do not invent impossible elemental knowledge or effects solely because two element names appear together. Specific Skills and established world rules take priority.

8.content:
POWER DETECTION:
A detection or appraisal ability reveals only what its explicit scope permits.

Seeing an unfamiliar ability does not automatically reveal its name, class, exact stats, mana cost, cooldown, hidden traits, limitations, source, rarity, or counters.

A basic Mana Sense may reveal facts such as presence, approximate intensity, direction, or an obvious elemental nature only when its skill definition permits those observations.

Exact mechanical information requires an ability that explicitly provides exact information.

A successful detection/appraisal check does not override secrecy, player-only System information, or NPC knowledge boundaries. The result becomes knowledge only for the character who actually performed or received that detection.

9.content:
DOMAIN MECHANICS — FIRST TRANSCENDENT / B-RANK LAYER

A Domain is a class- or creature-bound active authority field.
It is NOT an ordinary open-learn Skill and is NOT a passive once unlocked.

DOMAIN ACTIVATION:
- A Domain is inactive by default.
- Its owner consciously activates it like a special Skill/ability.
- Activation costs no MP, STA, or other normal resource.
- Activation does not consume the normal Main Action; it is a special Domain Activation that may be used once at the start of the owner's turn.
- The owner may voluntarily dismiss the Domain.
- Only one personal Domain may normally be active at a time.
- A Domain normally collapses when its owner is incapacitated.
- Domain activation has no Skill Proficiency and no Complexity progression unless later content explicitly defines Domain-specific mastery.

NASCENT B-RANK DOMAIN:
The standard first Domain is a Nascent Domain.
Default player reach = SHORT Range Band around the owner and moving with the owner.
Specific content may explicitly alter the Domain's Range Band.

UNIVERSAL LOWER-RANK SUPPRESSION:
While a B-rank Domain is active, a target below B-rank that lacks an equivalent Domain/Authority is qualitatively suppressed.

For a lower-rank creature inside the Domain:
- outgoing Modified Power ×0.65
- Hit Chance -15 percentage points
- the Domain owner gains ×1.20 outgoing Modified Power against that creature
- the Domain owner gains +15 percentage points Hit Chance against that creature

A lower-rank attack, projectile, spell, or other hostile effect created outside the Domain but entering the Domain to affect its owner is also subject to the ×0.65 Modified Power and -15 percentage-point Hit penalties where mechanically applicable.

Apply these Domain modifiers after the Skill's normal written power, Proficiency modifiers, and ordinary tactical modifiers, but before defense/resistance and final variance.

DOMAIN CLASH — SAME RANK:
When two B-rank Domain users oppose one another with active Domains, the universal lower-rank suppression does not apply between those B-rank users.
Their individual Domain Laws remain active according to their own text.
Do not invent an automatic 'stronger Domain wins' score in this version.

LOWER-RANK INTERACTION:
A lower-rank character cannot normally dispel, cancel, overwrite, or contest a B-rank Domain through ordinary lower-rank Skills.
An explicit Domain-countering, Authority, artifact, narrative exception, or later system rule may override this.

DOMAIN LAW:
Each evolved player Domain has a specific Law derived from the character's previous Class Passive and development path.
The Law is active only while the Domain is active.
The former passive is replaced by this controllable Domain Law rather than stacking separately.

Do not treat Half-Divine/B-rank status as a hidden universal stat multiplier.
Its qualitative advantage is represented by explicit B-rank growth, Gear/Skills, and the Domain rules above.

10.content:
CHECK GATE:
Do not roll merely because an action exists. Use a mechanical check only when BOTH are true:
1. the outcome is genuinely uncertain, and
2. success or failure has meaningful consequences.

Do NOT roll for routine actions, ordinary conversation, obvious observations, uncomplicated walking/travel, scene transitions, basic searches where nothing is concealed, or other low-stakes actions with no meaningful uncertainty.

CHECK TYPES:
1. Automatic: no roll when the result is obvious, uncontested, or effectively trivial.
2. Difficulty Check: Actor Score versus a fixed Difficulty Score.
3. Opposed Check: Actor Score versus another creature/effect's Opposition Score.

SCORES:
Actor Score = relevant Core Stat + explicit Skill/Technique bonus + explicit effect bonuses.
Opposition Score = relevant opposing Stat/Difficulty + explicit opposing Skill/Technique bonus + explicit effect bonuses.
Do not assume raw Skill Proficiency equals a check bonus unless that Skill explicitly converts proficiency into one.

SUCCESS CHANCE:
Chance% = Actor Score ÷ (Actor Score + Opposition Score) × 100.
Roll one d100. A roll less than or equal to Chance% succeeds.

If the power gap is so extreme that the outcome is effectively trivial, use Automatic resolution instead of forcing an artificial 1-in-20 style failure/success chance.

The Narrator may choose the relevant stat/skill from the actual attempted action, but must not choose whichever stat gives the desired story outcome.

11.content:
SITUATIONAL MODIFIERS:
Translate established circumstances into a small standardized modifier to the relevant Actor or Opposition Score.

Minor advantage/disadvantage: ±10%
Strong advantage/disadvantage: ±20%
Extreme advantage/disadvantage: ±35%

Multiple independent modifiers on the same side add before multiplication.
Example: Detection Score 30, daylight +10% and very quiet surroundings +10% => 30 × 1.20 = 36.

Do not invent arbitrary percentages. Use only modifiers justified by concrete circumstances.

STEALTH VS DETECTION:
Typical Stealth Score = AGI + explicit Stealth bonus.
Typical Detection Score = PER + explicit Awareness/Detection bonus.
Then apply situational modifiers and resolve as an Opposed Check.

Examples of context:
- bright daylight may aid Detection
- darkness/cover may aid Stealth
- very quiet surroundings may aid Detection
- heavy rain/crowd noise may hinder Detection
- rushing may hinder Stealth
- deliberate slow movement may aid Stealth when circumstances permit

PERCEPTION IS NOT OMNISCIENCE:
A successful perception, insight, tracking, or deception-related check reveals only evidence actually available through that action. It does not reveal hidden thoughts, System information, exact stats, secret skill names, narrator knowledge, or the objectively true explanation without evidence.

12.content:
LEVEL / XP
XP_TO_NEXT = Current Level × 100.

When XP reaches the threshold:
1. subtract that threshold and preserve carryover;
2. Level +1;
3. grant 5 free Stat Points unless an explicit rule changes this;
4. apply the current Base Class's automatic Favored-Stat growth defined by Content;
5. recalculate derived maxima;
6. repeat while carryover reaches the next threshold.

Level-up does not refill current HP/MP/STA unless an explicit effect does so.
Free Stat Points may be assigned to STR, VIT, AGI, INT, PER or WIL.
Meaningful rewards may grant XP; trivial repeat spam does not.

COMBAT XP FORMULA
Base XP = defeated target Level*10.
Rank-gap modifier versus player's Rank at encounter start: same x1; +1 x2; +2 x4; +3+ x8; -1 x0.5; -2 or lower x0.25.
Target type: Normal x1; Elite x1.5; Boss x2.5.
Final target XP = round(Base XP * Rank-gap * Target-type).

DEFEAT-XP LOCK
During Combat Initialization calculate each actual hostile's Final target XP ONCE from:
- that target's locked Level;
- that target's locked Rank;
- that target's locked Normal/Elite/Boss type;
- Alaric's Rank at encounter start.
Store it as FIXED `DefeatXP` for that encounter.
ACTIVE Combat never guesses, recalculates from prose, or changes DefeatXP.
On an eligible defeat, add exactly that locked DefeatXP once to Pending Combat XP.
Escaped targets contribute 0.

ELIGIBLE DEFEAT
Award eligibility exists when a real independent opponent/Monster is decisively defeated through death, explicit nonlethal incapacitation or finalized surrender/defeat. A legitimate wild-Monster hunt may qualify even if the Monster did not attack first.
No XP for helpless/captive/domesticated farming, already-defeated bodies, artificial repeat targets, or non-encounters without meaningful independent opposition.

PENDING-ONLY LOCK
During ACTIVE Combat record each eligible defeated target once into Pending Combat XP using its locked DefeatXP, but NEVER add it to persistent XP and NEVER trigger Level-Up while any hostile combatant remains active.
The terminal Combat End Loop verifies target uniqueness and awards the whole Pending total exactly once.

QUEST XP
Quest Base XP = Recommended Level*10. Minor/routine x1.5; Standard x2; Dangerous x3; Major/Dungeon/major objective x5. Quest XP is separate from Combat XP unless the Quest explicitly replaces it.

13.content:
LOOT RESOLUTION

Loot is physical world state.
Victory makes recoverable loot available; it does NOT automatically teleport loot into Inventory.

The player must actually take, receive, harvest, or otherwise acquire an item before the Tracker adds it to Inventory.

NON-HUMAN MONSTERS / NATIVE FAUNA:
Native fauna and other non-human Monsters normally carry no currency.
Their ordinary loot is made from physically or magically recoverable body/material profiles defined by Content. Faunal Monsters may yield ordinary physical materials such as hide, teeth, antlers/tusks, claws, meat, fat, bone or organs as appropriate.

Examples include:
- hide/pelt,
- fangs,
- claws,
- horns,
- tusks,
- scales,
- bone,
- glands,
- venom,
- spirit essence,
- other species-specific materials.

The condition of the body matters.
A destroyed horn cannot also be recovered intact.
Fire, disintegration, acid, crushing, or other combat consequences may damage or ruin materials.

Monster materials normally carry the same Rank as the defeated monster unless Content explicitly defines an exceptional material.

HUMANS:
Humans grant XP exactly like monsters, but ordinary Human loot is different.

A defeated Human may leave only what they were actually carrying or wearing:
- Copper/Silver/Gold,
- equipped weapon,
- equipped armor,
- equipped accessories,
- consumables,
- documents,
- keys,
- carried valuables,
- other established possessions.

Human currency is contextual, not generated by Rank.
A poor high-rank Human may carry little money; a wealthy low-rank Human may carry more.

GEAR PERSISTENCE:
Looted Gear is the same item instance the defeated owner used.
Preserve its Rank, ATK/MATK/DEF/MDEF, explicit effects, damage state, and identity.
Do not reroll or improve an item merely because it became loot.

A Human's learned Skills do not become loot.
A Skill Stone, manual, or similar Skill item is loot only if it physically existed in that person's possessions.

INTELLIGENT MONSTERS:
If Content or established story state says an intelligent monster carried Gear, currency, documents, or other possessions, those physical possessions may also be recoverable.
Do not invent carried valuables after defeat merely to increase rewards.



OFFICIAL COMBAT-END LOOT TIMING:
When an ACTIVE encounter ends, the [COMBAT END] protocol owns standard reward/loot resolution. It identifies what is physically recoverable before ordinary story play resumes. This creates availability only; ownership still requires an actual take/receive/harvest action. Items physically manipulated during combat remain governed by ordinary state/ownership rules and are not duplicated at Combat End.

REWARD RESOLUTION ORDER:
1. remain in ACTIVE Combat while any hostile combatant remains active; defeated opponents only accumulate Pending Combat XP;
2. at terminal COMBAT END, finalize all Defeated/Escaped opponents and verify Pending Combat XP once;
3. award the verified Pending Combat XP exactly once and resolve all Core Level-ups with carryover;
4. identify physically recoverable loot;
5. narrate what is available;
6. add only items/currency the player actually takes or receives to persistent state.

Do not silently convert monster materials into Gold.
Sale is a separate economic transaction.

14.content:
COIN TRANSACTIONS AND NORMALIZATION

Currency denomination ratios are setting facts from Lore. Under the current Avereth standard:
10 Copper = 1 Silver
10 Silver = 1 Gold
100 Copper = 1 Gold

For every monetary transaction that changes tracked Coin:
1. preserve the exact price already established by Lore, narration, contract, shop, quest, or prior state unless a legitimate in-world cause explicitly changes that price;
2. convert both the character's tracked Coin and the exact transaction amount to total Copper;
3. add or subtract the exact Copper value;
4. reject the transaction if the resulting total would be negative unless an explicit debt/credit rule is established;
5. normalize the remaining total back to Gold, Silver, and Copper using the ratios above;
6. update the tracker to that normalized result.

Example: 5 Silver = 50 Copper. Paying a 10-Copper fee leaves 40 Copper = 4 Silver exactly. No change is owed.

COIN INTEGRITY:
- Coin counts are whole integers. Do not create fractional Copper unless Lore explicitly introduces a smaller denomination.
- Do not invent change that the arithmetic does not produce.
- Do not silently alter an established fee to make a transaction work.
- A denomination mismatch may matter physically (for example, a 2-Copper toll when only Silver is carried). If exact change or exchange availability matters, resolve that as an in-world transaction; never fake the arithmetic.
- If narration, an NPC dossier, or a tracker contains an obvious arithmetic contradiction, the established denomination rules and exact transaction history control the corrected Coin total. Do not preserve an arithmetic error merely because it appeared earlier.

TRACKER REPAIR / NET-HOLDINGS RULE:
- The Coin tracker stores final net holdings after the entire exchange, not the previous tracker total plus received change.
- Change is part of the same transaction; it is not additional income.
- If the previous tracker conflicts with exact established transaction history, reconstruct the correct total from the last reliable holdings plus all established transactions, then write the corrected normalized total.
- Do not propagate a known arithmetic error merely because it is the most recent Character Sheet value.

WHOLE-COPPER PRICE RULE:
Every ordinary price, fee, wage, bounty, or reward must resolve to a whole-Copper amount under the active currency standard. Do not quote a fractional denomination that implies fractional Copper. Under 10 Copper = 1 Silver, "one quarter Silver" (=2.5 Copper) is invalid unless Lore later introduces a smaller denomination.

15.content:
CLASS FRAMEWORK
A Class is the character's major power path. Base Class selection may apply a one-time Level-1 growth package defined by Content.

Standard evolution milestones occur every 15 Levels: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90 unless explicit content says otherwise.
Evolution choices are generated from established development: repeated Skills/elements, weapon style, stat investment, role, training, major victories, discoveries and other meaningful history.

Do not award a specialized or rare evolution from one trivial use. Offer multiple plausible options when history supports them.
Evolution may add or transform passives, permissions, traits, Domains or other explicit mechanics, but it does not silently add universal HP/stat growth beyond rules actually written elsewhere.

Skills remain open-learn unless an explicit prerequisite says otherwise.

16.content:
SKILL STRUCTURE
A Skill defines only fields it needs: Rank, Complexity, Tags, Type, Power/scaling, ATK/MATK use, Cost, Range, Hit modifier and explicit Effects.

Rank = broad power band.
Complexity 1/2/3 = foundation / intermediate / advanced mechanical budget inside that Rank.
Proficiency = mastery of that specific Skill.
Class Affinity = learning speed only, not extra damage after learning.

LEARNING
Unknown Skills require a legitimate acquisition path and Learning Progress unless explicitly granted.
Base Learning Progress: C1 100; C2 200; C3 300.
Apply only the single highest applicable Class Affinity multiplier supplied by Content.

PROFICIENCY
Known Skills use P1-P5.
P1: written mechanics.
P2: Cost ×0.95.
P3: Cost ×0.95; attacks +5pp Hit; non-hit primary numeric effect ×1.05 when meaningful.
P4: Cost ×0.925; damaging Modified Power ×1.10; attacks retain +5pp Hit; comparable non-damage effect ×1.10.
P5: Cost ×0.90; damaging Modified Power ×1.15; attacks retain +5pp Hit; comparable non-damage effect ×1.15; Skill becomes evolution-eligible when its other conditions are met.
Milestone modifiers are totals, not cumulative products.

Proficiency Progress per promotion: C1 75; C2 100; C3 150.
Meaningful use/training may grant progress; trivial safe repetition grants 0.

SKILL EVOLUTION
P5 permits but does not guarantee evolution. The evolved Skill should follow how it was actually used/trained and remain recognizably descended from the prior technique unless a true transformation is established.

Numerical design of new Skills belongs to Content's Skill Design Rules, not Core.

17.content:
GEAR — v0.1 SIMPLIFIED MODEL:
Normal equipment does NOT modify STR, VIT, AGI, INT, PER, or WIL.

Gear contributes direct combat values only:
ATK = physical offensive equipment power
MATK = magical offensive equipment power
DEF = physical defensive equipment power added to Base DEF
MDEF = magical defensive equipment power added to Base MDEF

Typical use:
- physical weapons primarily grant ATK
- magical foci/staves primarily grant MATK
- armor grants DEF and/or MDEF
- accessories may grant any of ATK, MATK, DEF, or MDEF

Add equipped Gear ATK/MATK/DEF/MDEF directly to the character's derived combat values. Gear never requires recalculating Core Stats.

Special item effects may later grant explicit modifiers such as Fire Damage +10%, Crit +3 percentage points, or Mana Cost -5%, but only when written on the item. Do not translate ordinary gear into hidden Core Stat bonuses.

24.comment: [SKILLS] Acquisition, Affinity, and AI Skill Design
24.content:
SKILL ACQUISITION
Skills are open-learn, not class-exclusive. A new Skill needs a legitimate source: teacher, Skill Stone, reward/evolution, established self-development or another explicit source.
Starting Character Creation is the exception: choose exactly 2 starter Skills from the selected Base Class; Basic Attack is automatic.

DISCIPLINE AFFINITY
Use the single highest relevant multiplier:
Warrior — Martial 1.50, Defense 1.25, Arcane 0.75, otherwise 1.00.
Mage — Arcane 1.50, Control 1.25, Martial 0.75, otherwise 1.00.
Guardian — Defense 1.50, Martial 1.25, Precision/Mobility 0.90, Arcane 0.75, otherwise 1.00.
Duelist — Precision 1.50, Mobility/Martial 1.25, Arcane 0.75, otherwise 1.00.
Ranger — Precision 1.50, Mobility 1.25, Arcane 0.75, otherwise 1.00.
Affinity changes Learning/Proficiency progress only.

AI SKILL DESIGN — DO NOT USE PREBUILT HIGHER-RANK BANKS
Create Skills from established fiction when a valid acquisition path exists.
- First choose role, Rank, Complexity (1 foundation / 2 intermediate / 3 advanced), Tags, damage type and trade-offs.
- F-rank offensive P1 calibration:
  C1 Base 6-12, total stat coefficients about 1.25-1.90, Cost about 5-10.
  C2 Base 8-16, coefficients about 1.50-2.40, Cost about 8-16.
  C3 Base 10-18, coefficients about 1.75-2.60, Cost about 12-22.
- Pure single-target damage may spend most of its budget on Power. Accuracy, LONG range, extra Range-Band movement, AoE, multi-hit, penetration, defense, healing, control, reactions and high reliability consume that same budget.
- Use Core Range Bands only: ENGAGED / SHORT / MEDIUM / LONG. Do not generate meter-based combat ranges.
- Multi-hit splits its budget across strikes; AoE per-target output should normally be below a same-Complexity dedicated single-target technique.
- Higher-Rank Skills are generated from the closest existing technique and current same-Rank benchmarks. Keep similar stat coefficients when the technique relationship is unchanged; put most Rank growth into Base Power, Cost and/or explicit effects.
- Do not simultaneously inflate Base Power, scaling, range, accuracy, area and control with no trade-off.
- A normal new Skill should not trivially one-shot a healthy same-Rank peer without a major condition, drawback or exceptional premise.
- Fix the generated Skill once learned. Later changes require real Skill evolution, not silent rewriting.

25.comment: [MONSTER] Avereth Fauna, F-Rank Anchors, and Formula Scaling
25.content:
AVERETH MONSTER FAUNA
All native non-sapient fauna on the continent of Avereth are mechanically Monsters.
"Animal", "beast", "wolf", "deer", "horse", "boar", etc. describe ecology/body plan, NOT a separate non-Monster rules category.
Wild, domestic, docile and hostile fauna all have Level/Rank and use Monster mechanics.
Domestication or peaceful behavior does not turn a creature into a Human-stat character.

DIRECT-STAT MONSTER MODEL
Generic Monsters use only:
Level | Rank | HP | ATK | DEF | MDEF | Hit | Initiative | Attack Type | Attack Range Band.

They do NOT use STR/VIT/AGI/INT/PER/WIL, MP, STA, Character Crit, Classes, Skill Proficiency, a Movement stat or Gear unless an explicit authored profile specifically grants those systems.

Generic natural attack:
- Raw Power = ATK
- Base Hit Chance = Hit
- Crit:none
- no MP/STA cost
- Physical, Range ENGAGED unless the body-plan line says otherwise.

Generic Monsters use Core's universal normal one-band movement. Extra movement exists only when an explicit authored Skill/Trait says so.

RANK BANDS
F 1-14 | E 15-29 | D 30-44 | C 45-59 | B 60-74 | A 75-89 | S 90-104.
The same direct-stat formulas continue across Ranks; do not build separate numeric databases for E/D/C/B/A/S.
Most ordinary settled-region fauna are F-rank. Higher-Rank fauna are increasingly rare evolved Monsters, not a different mechanical species.

F1 BODY-PLAN ANCHORS
Format: HP / ATK / DEF / MDEF / Hit / Init | default natural attack

Rat / small vermin:
16 / 6 / 0 / 0 / 75 / 10 | Bite | Physical | ENGAGED

Wolf / canid:
23 / 9 / 0 / 0 / 80 / 12 | Bite | Physical | ENGAGED

Boar / wild pig:
41 / 11 / 2 / 0 / 70 / 7 | Gore | Physical | ENGAGED

Deer / elk / light hoofed:
27 / 7 / 0 / 0 / 65 / 14 | Kick/Antler | Physical | ENGAGED

Horse / large grazer:
38 / 8 / 1 / 0 / 68 / 12 | Kick | Physical | ENGAGED

Bear-like:
63 / 14 / 2 / 1 / 70 / 5 | Claw/Bite | Physical | ENGAGED

Feline predator:
30 / 10 / 0 / 0 / 82 / 13 | Claw/Bite | Physical | ENGAGED

Serpent / snake-like:
20 / 8 / 0 / 1 / 78 / 11 | Bite | Physical | ENGAGED

Raptor / predatory bird:
18 / 7 / 0 / 0 / 78 / 15 | Talons/Beak | Physical | ENGAGED
Flight is ecological access/positioning; it does not grant extra Range-Band movement unless an explicit capability says so.

Arthropod / insectoid:
24 / 8 / 2 / 0 / 72 / 8 | Bite/Sting | Physical | ENGAGED

Aquatic predator:
36 / 11 / 1 / 0 / 75 / 10 | Bite | Physical | ENGAGED
This body-plan assumes functional movement in water. Do not invent a hidden numeric movement penalty/bonus from terrain; use only established environmental or explicit mechanics.

Goblin-like:
45 / 11 / 1 / 1 / 75 / 8 | Natural/unarmed strike | Physical | ENGAGED
If a real individual visibly carries Gear, authored Gear may replace/modify the attack normally.

Ogre-like:
90 / 18 / 2 / 0 / 60 / 3 | Slam | Physical | ENGAGED

Armored Beast:
70 / 12 / 5 / 1 / 70 / 5 | Body strike/Bite | Physical | ENGAGED

Spirit:
40 / 14 / 0 / 5 / 80 / 10 | Magical discharge | Magical | MEDIUM

LEVEL SCALING
Let g = Level - 1.

HP = round(HP1 × (1 + 0.20g))
ATK = round(ATK1 × (1 + 0.22g))
DEF = max(0, round((DEF1 + 1) × (1 + 0.20g) - 1))
MDEF = max(0, round((MDEF1 + 1) × (1 + 0.20g) - 1))
Hit = min(95, Hit1 + 2×floor(g/15))
Init = round(Init1 × (1 + 0.05g))

Rank is determined by Level band after scaling.
Do not apply an additional hidden Rank multiplier on top of these formulas.

F-RANK ENCOUNTER LEVEL SELECTION
Use an already-authored/Quest/area Level when one exists.
If a natural encounter is generated without an established Level:
- settled road/farm/town outskirts: Level 1;
- ordinary nearby wilderness: F1-F3;
- explicitly remote/deep dangerous wilderness: F4-F7;
- explicitly established dangerous F-rank hunting/Quest territory: use its established range, never above F14.
If the area's danger is not established, use F1.

Choose/roll inside an allowed band without using appearance as the reason.
Large size, scars, old age, aggression, calmness, unusual coloration or "looks dangerous" never independently raise Level.

INDIVIDUAL VARIATION
After Level scaling, ordinary individuals may vary:
- HP/ATK roughly ±20%;
- DEF/MDEF ±1;
- Hit ±5 percentage points;
- Initiative ±2;
only when established body condition/size reasonably supports it.

Variation changes the individual, not its Level/Rank.
Fix all values once instantiated.

NO FREE TRAITS
Normal generic Monsters receive no invented Skills, Traits, resource pools, Crit, enrages, wound phases, combo attacks, armor passives, movement exceptions or status mechanics merely from narration.
A scarred boar is still the Boar profile unless an explicit authored Elite/Boss/special profile says otherwise.

HIGHER-RANK EVOLUTION — FEW RULES, NOT DATABASES
Direct stats continue the same formulas through E-S.
At a real Rank evolution, an authored or narratively established Monster MAY gain a species-fitting evolved capability; it is not automatic.
Use restraint:
- E/D: normally at most one defining evolved capability at a time unless explicitly authored;
- C/A: additional coherent capabilities may emerge through established evolution/history;
- B+: a Domain becomes possible under Core rules when established;
- S: remains exceptional and setting-significant.
Never generate abilities specifically to counter Alaric.

UNLISTED SPECIES
Use the nearest ecological/body-plan F1 anchor, then Level scaling and bounded individual variation.
Fix the resulting direct-stat profile for the encounter.

PROFILE INSTANTIATION TIMING
Mere sight, tracks, hunting, or non-hostile observation does not require a full combat profile.
Instantiate/fix exact mechanical Monster values when mechanics actually need them (Combat START, explicit appraisal/system inspection, or another real mechanical interaction).
Once instantiated for an encounter, copy the locked profile forward; never reroll Level/variation each round.

26.content:
ELITE / BOSS MONSTER DESIGN
Elite and Boss are encounter types layered onto a valid fixed Monster profile; they are not separate species databases.

DESIGNATION LOCK
Do not infer Elite/Boss from mere size, scars, age, aggression, reputation-flavored prose or because a fight should be dramatic.
Elite/Boss status must be explicitly authored, established by a Quest/area/encounter premise, or intentionally generated as the encounter type before Combat resolution.

DEFAULT MODIFIERS after normal Level scaling and individual variation:
Elite: HP ×1.75; ATK ×1.15; DEF/MDEF ×1.10; Hit +5pp; Init +2.
Boss: HP ×2.50; ATK ×1.30; DEF/MDEF ×1.20; Hit +5pp; Init +3.
Round final direct stats and fix them.

An Elite may gain one explicit defining species-fitting Trait/attack/reaction.
A Boss may gain several coherent mechanics tied to species, environment, Dungeon role or established history.
Do not add abilities merely to counter the player.

All such mechanics must be explicit in the fixed profile before first use.
At B-rank and above, an exceptional Monster may receive a Domain when established; use Core Domain rules.

Recoverable materials depend on actual species/body state and are never auto-collected.

27.comment: [GEAR] F-Rank References and Linear Rank Scaling
27.content:
GEAR MODEL
Gear has a Rank and fixed item-instance values. Normal Gear directly contributes ATK/MATK/DEF/MDEF; it does not alter Core Stats unless an exceptional item explicitly says so.

F-RANK REFERENCE
Martial Weapon ATK 4-10
Arcane Focus MATK 4-10
Light Armor DEF 2-4, MDEF 2-5
Heavy Armor DEF 5-8, MDEF 1-3
Shield/secondary defensive slot DEF 3-5, MDEF 2-4

HIGHER-RANK GENERATION
Let RankIndex R: F=0, E=1, D=2, C=3, B=4, A=5, S=6.
For ordinary higher-Rank Gear, start from an appropriate F reference/item and use:
Ranked combat value ≈ round(F value × (1 + 0.75R)).
Choose/fix the actual item value once. Exceptional named/enchanted artifacts may deviate through explicit effects instead of a universal rarity ladder.

Typical slots:
Warrior weapon + heavy armor; Mage focus + light armor; Guardian weapon + heavy armor + shield; Duelist weapon + light armor; Ranger weapon + light armor.
Generic monsters do not use Gear unless the individual actually carries/equips it.

28.content:
CLASS EVOLUTION DESIGN
Rank milestones are Level 15/30/45/60/75/90 for E/D/C/B/A/S.

Do not maintain a prewritten database of later Class paths. At a milestone, generate 2-4 plausible options from the character's actual history: dominant Skills/elements, weapon style, stat investment, combat role, repeated tactics, training, discoveries, major victories and meaningful choices.

A standard evolution:
- preserves the Base Class and learned Skills unless its text explicitly transforms something;
- may grant or transform one coherent passive/permission/trait appropriate to the new Rank;
- may make certain future Skill designs more natural;
- does not automatically grant extra universal Stat or HP growth beyond Core's Level + Base-Class growth;
- remains mechanically specific once chosen.

Example themes are prompts, not fixed menus:
Warrior may evolve toward aggression, weapon mastery or vanguard defense.
Mage may specialize by element, arcane structure or control.
Guardian may deepen protection, retaliation or battlefield control.
Duelist may deepen precision, mobility or counterplay.
Ranger may deepen marksmanship, hunting/control or mobility.

At B-rank, an established evolution may manifest a Domain using Core Domain rules. Rare evolutions require rare established conditions rather than random rarity inflation.

29.content:
TRANSMIGRATION STARTER KITS — ONE-TIME CAMPAIGN INITIALIZATION

When System Character Creation is completed by selecting one Base Class and exactly 2 Base Skills, the System grants exactly one matching F-rank starter kit.
This is a one-time bootstrap benefit, not a repeatable Shop or Skill.

All listed values are fixed item-instance values.

- Starter Heavy Armor [F]: DEF 6, MDEF 2

COMMON BOOTSTRAP ITEMS:

- 5 Silver

CREATION-COMPLETION EFFECT:
After the Class is chosen and exactly 2 Base Skills from that Class are chosen:

2. grant/preserve the selected Class's Basic Attack at Proficiency 1, Progress 0, plus the 2 selected Base Skills at Proficiency 1, Progress 0;
3. materialize and equip the matching starter kit;
4. preserve Simple Traveler's Clothes as ordinary clothing unless the player later discards/replaces them;
5. mark the one-time starter kit as claimed.

No later Class Evolution or Class change grants another starter kit unless an explicit future rule says so.

30.content:
AVERETH
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Civilizations, species, religions and dynasties have risen and vanished over immense history; some ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as myth.

Tone is high fantasy with contrast: safe cities, trade, families and festivals coexist with dangerous wilderness, Dungeons, political violence and old powers. The setting is not uniformly grim.

Current campaign scope defines six human kingdoms, two monster realms, the neutral Adventurers' Guild and independent high-rank actors. More great powers may exist but remain undefined until play needs them.
Human and monster states are not unified blocs and may trade, ally, feud or fight across species lines.

Material baseline: Western-fantasy medieval society alongside mana and high magic; modern/industrial technology is not assumed.

31.content:
PUBLIC POWER KNOWLEDGE
Ordinary society broadly understands Level, Rank, Class, Skills, Skill Proficiency and Evolution.
Exact Levels require measurement (commonly Guild/temple methods); exact Core Stat numbers are not normally visible.

Most humans receive a Base Class around adulthood. Class reflects affinity rather than an absolute Skill prohibition.
Rank corresponds socially to Evolution stage: F Base, E first evolution, D second, C third, B Half-Divine, A higher Transcendent, S Full-Divine.
Standard evolution concepts are known; rare conditions are valuable secrets often held by powerful families, temples or institutions.

32.content:
MANA / LEARNING
Mana is a normal part of Avereth and can support minor everyday uses as well as combat magic.
Ordinary formal Skills are most commonly learned from teachers or Skill Stones; experimentation alone is not the normal path for most people.

Schools and specialist academies exist. Nobles, wealthy families, militaries, temples, Adventurer families and scholarship students have better access to elite training.
Avereth does not normally use cultivation-style Sects; great houses, royal lines, temples, military lineages and old magical families fill similar institutional niches and often guard teachers, Skill Stones, rare Evolution knowledge, Gear and records.

33.content:
EVOLUTION / LIFESPAN
Evolution improves health and longevity as well as power. Broad natural lifespans:
F ~100-120y; E ~150-180y; D ~250-350y; C ~500-700y; B ~2,000-3,000y; A ~10,000-20,000y; S 100,000y+.
These are tendencies, not protection from violence or exceptional causes.

SOCIAL POWER
Most people remain F/E. D-ranks are respected specialists/local elites; C-ranks are major regional figures; B-ranks often occupy senior institutional roles. A-ranks are rare strategic figures; S-ranks are kingdom-level deterrents.
Wealth strongly affects training access below the highest ranks, but cannot indefinitely substitute for personal power.
Exact high-rank populations are uncertain because independents and hidden individuals exist.

34.content:
ADVENTURERS' GUILD
A neutral transnational Guild operates across recognized human kingdoms and has limited formal contact with monster realms.
It handles registration, Level/Rank certification, quests, monster/Dungeon information, rewards, material brokerage, frontier support and high-rank mediation.
Its strength is network, legitimacy, information and economic reach; it does not casually command every powerful Adventurer.

JURISDICTION BOUNDARY
The Guild does NOT replace local rulers, civil authorities, courts, town/city guards, militaries, property law or ordinary criminal law.
Its authority comes from contracts, certification, information networks, negotiated privileges and the willingness of states/communities to recognize its functions.
Local law and Guild rules may overlap, cooperate or conflict depending on established circumstances.

35.content:
MONSTER ECOLOGY / FAUNA
On Avereth, native non-sapient fauna are part of the Monster ecology.
A wolf, deer, horse, boar, bear, bird or other familiar animal-shaped creature is mechanically a Monster with Level and Rank even when peaceful, domesticated or ecologically ordinary.
"Animal" remains normal everyday language for body type/ecology; it does not indicate a separate non-Monster rules category.

Monster classification is mechanical/ecological, NOT a synonym for hostility.
Ordinary domesticated F-rank fauna may fill the same everyday roles as livestock, mounts, hunting animals and pets where appropriate.

Monsters are natural populations, not temporary game spawns.
They reproduce, compete, migrate, establish territories/social structures, are hunted or domesticated, and may evolve through Ranks.
Most ordinary fauna around settled regions are F-rank. Higher-Rank evolved specimens become progressively rarer and more dangerous.

Sapience is separate from Monster classification.
Many Monsters are non-sapient fauna; others can speak, organize societies, rule territory and conduct diplomacy.

Elite = an explicitly exceptional individual/encounter type.
Boss = a practical label for an exceptional Dungeon-centered or encounter-defining threat, not necessarily a separate species.

36.content:
CURRENT GREAT-POWER MAP
Human kingdoms: Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion, Duskreach.
Monster realms: Ashen Scale Dominion, Verdant Fang Court.
Additional states may exist; borders, minor states, cities, noble holdings and most history stay open until needed.

There is no permanent human-vs-monster bloc. Trade, rivalry, border conflict, non-aggression and temporary alliances all occur.

HIGH-RANK DETERRENCE
S-ranks are strategic actors, not routine battlefield units. Direct clashes risk catastrophic collateral damage and escalation, so they usually act through deterrence, diplomacy, representatives or only truly strategic intervention.
B/A-ranks handle much of the practical high-level conflict. A powerful ruler does not intervene merely because an unrelated lower-rank member of the same species/faction was killed.

37.content:
VALEDORN CROWN

Position: central Avereth.
Capital: Crownheart.
Status: strongest human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 3.

Identity:
Valedorn is the political center of human diplomacy and hosts the most influential royal court on the continent.
It possesses deep noble lineages, wealthy academies, old military institutions, and one of the largest Adventurers' Guild headquarters.

Its strength comes less from a single specialty than from having almost everything at a high level: wealth, population, military organization, magic, diplomacy, and several Full-Divine protectors.

Valedorn is powerful but not automatically dominant over every neighbor; coalitions of other kingdoms can still constrain it.

38.content:
CAELRETH

Position: western Avereth.
Capital: Asterhall.
Status: top-tier human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
Caelreth is the continent's most academically arcane human kingdom.
It is known for magical colleges, Skill-Stone study, enchantment research, ritual theory, and old mage families.

Caelreth's nobles heavily protect rare Evolution knowledge.
Its cities contain unusually dense populations of professional mages and high-rank researchers.

Relations with the Verdant Fang Court are cautious but often scholarly and commercial rather than purely hostile.

39.content:
VEYRHOLD

Position: eastern Avereth.
Capital: Ironward.
Status: top-tier martial kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
Veyrhold is a heavily militarized frontier kingdom shaped by centuries of dangerous borders.
Martial training, disciplined officer corps, fortified cities, and monster-hunting traditions are central to its culture.

It has the most openly tense relationship with the Ashen Scale Dominion.
Border clashes occur, but both sides avoid escalation that could draw their S-ranks into direct war.

40.content:
SOLMERE

Position: southern coast.
Capital: Goldharbor.
Status: major kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 1.

Identity:
Solmere is Avereth's largest maritime trade power.
Ports, shipyards, merchant houses, mercenary contracts, Dungeon imports, and inter-kingdom commerce dominate its politics.

It is less militarily imposing than Valedorn or Veyrhold but can buy expertise, logistics, and high-rank service at enormous scale.

Solmere maintains pragmatic trade across both human and monster polities and is one of the human states most comfortable dealing openly with intelligent monster populations.

41.content:
ILYRION

Position: south-central riverlands.
Capital: Sanctum Vale.
Status: major kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 1.

Identity:
Ilyrion is famous for temples, healers, soul rites, pilgrimage routes, and religious scholarship.
Many of Avereth's best-known resurrection specialists train or serve here.

The kingdom is not a theocracy, but temples possess major political and economic influence.

Several ancient faiths associated with historically famous S-rank figures or traditions maintain important sanctuaries in Ilyrion.

42.content:
DUSKREACH

Position: southeastern marches.
Capital: Blackgate.
Status: regional human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: none.

Identity:
Duskreach is a hard frontier realm with strong B- and A-rank military figures but no known Full-Divine protector.

It survives through fortifications, alliances, Guild contracts, mercenary service, and careful diplomacy with stronger neighbors.

Its rulers are acutely aware that wealth and armies cannot fully substitute for an S-rank at the kingdom level.

43.content:
ASHEN SCALE DOMINION

Position: volcanic eastern highlands.
Seat of power: the Cinder Throne.
Status: strongest recognized monster realm.
Public S-ranks: 3.

Identity:
The Dominion is ruled by ancient draconic and scaled bloodlines alongside other fire- and mountain-adapted monster species.

Its oldest rulers think in centuries rather than years.
Strength, bloodline, territory, oath, and personal authority matter more than human-style bureaucracy.

The Dominion is Veyrhold's most dangerous neighbor.
Neither side seeks a war large enough to force direct S-rank confrontation.

44.content:
VERDANT FANG COURT

Position: ancient western forests.
Seat of power: Thornheart.
Status: top-tier monster realm.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
The Court is a loose but ancient polity of powerful beast lineages, transformed predators, forest spirits, and other intelligent woodland species.

It is called a Court because status is negotiated through territory, lineage, favors, challenges, and old pacts rather than a human-style crown.

Its relations with Caelreth include trade, magical research, territorial disputes, and occasional cooperation against shared threats.

45.content:
SYSTEM COMMAND ROUTER — HARD RULE

A System command is invoked only when the FIRST non-whitespace character of the player's message is '#'.

Examples:
#status
#skills

57.content:
CURRENCY / EVERYDAY ECONOMY
Common currency: 10 Copper = 1 Silver; 10 Silver = 1 Gold.
Coins are whole units; the current standard has no fractional Copper.

Legal trade may include Skill Stones, Gear, magical tools, monster/Dungeon materials, healing, transport, training, maps and information.
Prices are intentionally local/contextual rather than fixed in Lore.

58.content:
NATURAL DUNGEONS
Natural Dungeons are persistent supernatural ecosystems/resource zones shaped by concentrated mana and other established local conditions.
They can contain unusual environments, rare materials, Skill Stones and exceptional Monsters.
They are physical/world locations, not temporary game instances that appear only for Alaric.
Exact Dungeon rules, layouts, ownership and local history remain open until established.

59.content:
DEATH / RESURRECTION
Death is socially real.
Powerful temples or specialists can sometimes perform rare, extremely expensive soul-return rituals through high magic.
Resurrection is not routine medical care and ordinary people cannot assume access to it.
Exact limits, prices, eligibility and formulas remain undefined until relevant.

60.comment: [LORE] Medieval Material Culture, Communication, and Travel
60.content:
MATERIAL CULTURE
Avereth uses a Western-fantasy medieval material baseline alongside mana and high magic.
Ordinary life relies on handcraft, smithing, mills, farms, carts, horses, sailing ships, fortified settlements, markets, written records and similar pre-industrial institutions.
Mana and high magic can accomplish things mundane medieval technology cannot, but this has NOT created a modern or industrial technological society.

Do not assume modern/industrial infrastructure or devices such as electrical grids, telephones, computers, engines, railways, mass industrial manufacturing or firearms unless later canon explicitly establishes an exception.

COMMUNICATION
Ordinary people communicate at distance through letters, messengers, couriers and travelers.
Magical long-distance communication is possible through sufficiently powerful magic, institutions or artifacts, but it is uncommon and not universal everyday infrastructure available to ordinary people on demand.

TRAVEL
Ordinary travel is by foot, mount, wagon/carriage and ship as geography permits.
Long-distance travel takes meaningful in-world time; do not compress cities or kingdoms together merely for narrative convenience.
Teleportation or comparable magical transport may exist when explicitly established, but is never assumed to be ordinary public transportation.

61.content:
SYSTEM QUERY KNOWLEDGE GUARD
All # commands are private read-only System queries unless a command explicitly says otherwise. They do not advance story time or Combat turns.
Use only Core, player-owned/known Content, the latest legitimate tracker, player-visible Quest/mechanical facts and established System notices.
Do NOT reveal narrator-only NPC secrets, hidden loot/branches/locations, undiscovered evolutions, future events or unidentified properties.

#combat EXCEPTION: during an already-instantiated PENDING/ACTIVE encounter, #combat may expose the locked mechanics required to audit that encounter (current HP/resources, direct combat stats, Initiative, Range Bands, locked actions). This remains private System information and does not become NPC knowledge. It never exposes biography, motives, uninstantiated future abilities or hidden loot.

Hypothetical calculations never mutate state. If required information is unknown, say so rather than inventing it.
